rationale: X correctly grounds the collision split in the shared Rails generator entry point and Thor's different create and revoke actions, and its direct probe confirms identical, force, skip, interactive no, EOF, and revoke outcomes. It covers every requested actor, non-goal, acceptance boundary, and intentionality question while avoiding an implementation or test prescription. Compared with the references, it is terser and its opening language briefly sounds as though a unified generate/destroy policy has already been selected, but the conditional acceptance examples and final questions clearly keep that product decision open. Its factual claims agree with the checkout and focused Railties tests, so there is no material error and it is at parity overall.

shortcomings.summary: The opening and working-model language leans toward a unified policy before intentionality has been established.
shortcomings.evidence: .amp/judge-inputs/L50/X.md:1-3 and 9 say to keep the commands inverse and establish one shared contract, including flags and answers meaning the same thing. Lines 15-31, 33, and 45-47 then correctly leave removal after identical/skip, destroy prompting, force semantics, and the create-versus-remove interpretation open; the conclusion is therefore somewhat rhetorically inconsistent but not actually locked in.

shortcomings.summary: The executable collision probe uses a minimal Thor generator rather than an actual application and nested-engine bin/rails workflow.
shortcomings.evidence: .amp/judge-inputs/L50/X.thread.md:531-550 runs a Thor::Group create/revoke probe and verifies its file results, while X.md:35 and 43 acknowledge that real engine workflows remain evidence to collect. The Rails command/root and engine behavior were still inspected, so this is a narrower verification gap than leaving the collision mechanics untested.

shortcomings.summary: It omits one useful observed CLI detail emphasized by both references: destroy help advertises generate-oriented force and skip descriptions even though revoke ignores them for files.
shortcomings.evidence: X.md:7 and 19-21 accurately describe destroy's current flag behavior but do not mention the shared help text. railties/lib/rails/generators.rb:171-181 shows that both command help paths list force as overwrite and skip as skip-existing; R1.md:31-35,116-128 and R2.md:17-20,25-31 surface this as evidence relevant to whether the difference is intentional.

strengths.summary: The current-behavior account is correct and supported by both source inspection and an executed collision probe.
strengths.evidence: .amp/judge-inputs/L50/X.thread.md:417-456 reads Thor create/revoke and prompt handling, and lines 531-550 execute cases showing conflict plus no leaves OLD, identical leaves NEW, force replaces, skip leaves OLD, EOF overwrites, and revoke removes. This matches Thor actions/create_file.rb:73-95, actions/empty_directory.rb:56-60, and shell/basic.rb:207-229 in the installed dependency.

strengths.summary: X accurately traces shared generator resolution, fallbacks, destination roots, and missing-generator behavior across generate and destroy.
strengths.evidence: railties/lib/rails/commands/generate/generate_command.rb:17-26 and destroy/destroy_command.rb:18-25 both call Rails::Generators.invoke with Rails::Command.root and differ only in invoke versus revoke behavior. railties/lib/rails/generators.rb:236-278 and 292-305 implement shared namespace/fallback lookup and the generate-help not-found message, while railties/lib/rails/command.rb:101-112 selects ENGINE_ROOT; `cd railties && bin/test test/generators_test.rb` passed 32 runs and 80 assertions.

strengths.summary: The brief covers the complete requested matrix while keeping consequential policy choices explicitly conditional.
strengths.evidence: .amp/judge-inputs/L50/X.md:13-31 covers identical and differing content, force, skip, yes/no/all/quit, EOF, nested engine roots, namespaced/fallback lookup, missing generators, and destroy-after-skip. Lines 37-45 identify the evidence and open questions needed to distinguish intentional create/remove semantics from accidental inconsistency, and lines 11 and 33 avoid implementation-oriented scope.

strengths.summary: Focused checkout verification supports the migration and engine claims that supplement the generic-file probe.
strengths.evidence: `cd railties && bin/test test/generators/create_migration_test.rb` passed 12 runs and 35 assertions, covering identical, force, skip, and revoke behavior. `cd railties && bin/test test/railties/generators_test.rb -n '/namespaced_when_engine|not_namespaced_when_engine/'` passed 7 runs and 32 assertions, supporting X.md:25's mountable versus non-mountable namespacing claim.
